saints.name: The Holy Innocents
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The children of Bethlehem slain by Herod in his rage against the newborn King, the first to die for Christ…
biography: The Gospel of Matthew records that Herod the Great, deceived by the wise men, sent and slew all the boys of Bethlehem and its borders from two years old and under, fulfilling the prophet Jeremias: 'A voice in Rama was heard... Rachel bewailing her children.' The Holy Family had already fled into Egypt at an angel's warning.

The Greek liturgy numbers the slain at 14,000, the Syrians at 64,000, medieval writers at 144,000; but Bethlehem was small, and modern commentators reckon the victims between six and twenty. Josephus does not record the deed, so slight was it beside Herod's other cruelties.

The Church venerates these children as martyrs — flores martyrum, the first flowers of the Church, in the hymn of Prudentius. St. Augustine says they died not only for Christ but in His stead: martyrs by blood alone, confessing Him not by speaking but by dying.

Their feast first appears, with those of St. Stephen and St. John, in the Leonine Sacramentary about 485; the West keeps it on 28 December, within the Christmas octave, and England called it Childermas. As the first to die for Christ, they are patrons of infants and children.
saints.knownFor: The infant martyrs of Bethlehem, first to die for Christ.
